milestones.title: Learn programming basics (Python or C++)
milestones.why: Every technical role starts here: variables, loops, functions.

milestones.title: Programming: OOP, files, libraries, debugging
milestones.why: You need to write real programs, not just small exercises.

milestones.title: Programming: clean code, testing, one language in depth
milestones.why: Interviews and jobs expect strong command of one language.

milestones.title: DSA basics: arrays, strings, recursion, complexity
milestones.why: Problem-solving is the base of every coding round.

milestones.title: DSA: stacks, trees, graphs, sorting - solve 100+ problems
milestones.why: Most companies test these topics in online assessments.

milestones.title: DSA: dynamic programming, hard problems, contests
milestones.why: Product companies ask medium-to-hard problems.

milestones.title: HTML and CSS: build 3 static pages
milestones.why: The foundation of anything shown in a browser.

milestones.title: JavaScript and DOM: build interactive pages
milestones.why: Makes your pages dynamic; required before any framework.

milestones.title: React: build a component-based app
milestones.why: Most web jobs ask for React or a similar framework.

milestones.title: Backend basics: Node.js/Express or Flask
milestones.why: Your app needs a server that handles requests.

milestones.title: Build REST APIs with a database and login
milestones.why: Real apps store data and have users.

milestones.title: Deploy a full-stack app live (Vercel/Render)
milestones.why: A live demo link is far stronger than code on a laptop.

milestones.title: SQL basics: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY
milestones.why: Almost every role uses databases.

milestones.title: SQL: joins, subqueries, window functions
milestones.why: Joins are asked in most interviews.

milestones.title: SQL: query optimization and real datasets
milestones.why: Needed for analyst and data-heavy roles.

milestones.title: Git and GitHub basics: commit, push, branch
milestones.why: Every team uses version control.

milestones.title: Git: pull requests, merge conflicts, open-source contribution
milestones.why: Shows you can work in a team and contribute beyond solo commits.

milestones.title: Git workflows and CI pipelines (GitHub Actions)
milestones.why: Core skill for DevOps roles.

milestones.title: Statistics basics: mean, variance, probability
milestones.why: The language of data and ML.

milestones.title: Statistics: distributions, hypothesis tests
milestones.why: Needed to draw correct conclusions from data.

milestones.title: Applied statistics and A/B testing on real data
milestones.why: Analyst roles are judged on this.

milestones.title: Machine learning intro: regression, classification
milestones.why: First step into ML.

milestones.title: ML models: trees, SVM, evaluation, scikit-learn
milestones.why: You must be able to train and evaluate models.

milestones.title: End-to-end ML project: data to deployed model
milestones.why: ML jobs value complete projects over theory.

milestones.title: System design basics: client-server, databases, APIs
milestones.why: You need the vocabulary before the case studies.

milestones.title: System design: caching, load balancing, scaling
milestones.why: Asked in interviews for experienced candidates.

milestones.title: System design case studies (URL shortener, chat app)
milestones.why: Product-company interviews include design rounds.

milestones.title: Cloud basics: compute, storage, networking
milestones.why: Most software now runs on the cloud.

milestones.title: Earn a cloud certification (AWS/Azure/GCP fundamentals)
milestones.why: A certificate is verifiable proof for your resume.

milestones.title: Docker, Kubernetes and Linux for deployment
milestones.why: Core daily tools for DevOps roles.

milestones.title: Aptitude basics: percentages, ratios, time and work
milestones.why: First round of most campus drives.

milestones.title: Aptitude + logical reasoning practice sets
milestones.why: Speed and accuracy decide cut-offs.

milestones.title: Full-length aptitude mock tests
milestones.why: Builds exam stamina and time management.

milestones.title: Communication basics: speaking and email writing
milestones.why: You will explain your work to others every day.

milestones.title: Group discussion and HR interview practice
milestones.why: Many campus drives have GD and HR rounds.

milestones.title: Present a project demo in front of an audience
milestones.why: Confident presentation sets you apart.

milestones.title: Build one mini project and put it on GitHub
milestones.why: Proof that you can build things.

milestones.title: Build a major project with real users or real data
milestones.why: Recruiters ask about projects in almost every interview.

milestones.title: Build a capstone project with live demo and write-up
milestones.why: A polished flagship project can carry your resume.

milestones.title: Join a technical club or committee
milestones.why: Peers, mentors and early exposure.

milestones.title: Take part in a hackathon
milestones.why: Teamwork under pressure, plus a story for interviews.

milestones.title: Lead or organise a campus event
milestones.why: Shows leadership and ownership.

milestones.title: Build an ATS-friendly resume and LinkedIn profile
milestones.why: Your resume decides if you even get a first call.

milestones.title: Apply for a summer internship
milestones.why: Internships are the strongest route to full-time offers.

milestones.title: Give mock technical and HR interviews
milestones.why: Practice under real conditions before the real thing.

milestones.title: Track and apply to company drives
milestones.why: Placement season is the time to apply widely.

milestones.title: Prepare for higher-studies exams (GATE/GRE) and applications
milestones.why: Your goal is higher studies, so exam preparation starts early.

milestones.title: RGPV / semester scoring plan for core subjects
milestones.why: Internals and end-sem scores keep TPO shortlists and higher-studies options open.

milestones.title: Time management and weekly habit tracker
milestones.why: Technical output only sticks if study habits and rest scale with it.

milestones.title: Complete one free cert or NPTEL audit that matches your role
milestones.why: A finished certificate proves follow-through on your resume.

milestones.title: Add tests and a simple CI check to one project
milestones.why: Teams expect you to catch regressions before they ship.

milestones.title: Web security basics: OWASP top 10 for your apps
milestones.why: Security headers and common flaws matter for web and full-stack roles.

milestones.title: Portfolio polish: two case studies with live demos
milestones.why: Recruiters skim case studies and live links before reading the rest of the resume.
